inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted at 2026-09-27: 220.287M issued less 80.173M treasury = 140.114M basic outstanding, plus 1.7M dilutive awards (Q3 FY2026 10-Q EPS note, treasury-stock method) = 141.8M. Held FLAT because SBC (incl. withholding taxes) is fully expensed in the flows. Q4 FY2026 buybacks (target raised to $400M for the year, $149.3M done through 9M) will shrink the count further, but under the charge-once rule they are the mechanism that keeps the count flat, not extra value.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $80.4M + payments related to tax withholding for share-based compensation $23.7M (financing) = $104.1M. Hasbro publishes no combined SBC-incl-taxes line in its filings, so the two lines are summed. 9M FY2026 run-rate is higher ($68.5M + $46.9M = $115.4M), hence sbc_pct_path starts at 2.6%.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD WACC. Risk-free ~4.2% (10y UST), ERP 5.0%, beta ~1.0 -> cost of equity ~9.2%. Pre-tax cost of debt ~5.5% (fixed-rate notes, 3.5-6.6% coupons), ~4.3% after tax. Market cap ~$16.9B vs debt $3.5B -> D/V ~17%. WACC ~8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all scenarios: Magic concentration risk is carried in the bear path and its 20% weight, not as a rate premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP operating leases (PV $339.6M at 2026-09-27): rent sits inside operating expense and therefore inside adjusted EBITDA, so lease cash is in the flows. Lease liabilities are NOT added to net debt (one treatment only). No finance leases disclosed.
inputs.nci_treatment: Noncontrolling interests $24.6M (book, 2026-09-27) deducted in equity_bridge; NCI share of earnings is ~$2-3M/yr, immaterial to the flows.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build (routing table: US operating company -- toys, tabletop/digital gaming, IP licensing; not a bank/REIT/holdco; no prior HAS valuation in MEMORY.md). FY0 = FY2025 (last completed fiscal year); year 1 = FY2026 built to the raised Q3 FY2026 guidance (7-9% cc revenue growth, adj. EBITDA $1.575-1.625B, capex ~$250M); 9 of its 12 months are already reported, which is why all three scenarios sit close together in year 1. REPORTED FCF CORRECTION: the Metrics CSV free_cash_flow ($829.9M FY2025) is OCF less PP&E additions only and omits 'Additions to software development' ($135.0M FY2025, $110.3M FY2024), which is real capex (capitalised digital-game and platform development; FY2023 10-K reported the two together as $209.3M PP&E additions). reported_fcf here = OCF 893.2 - PP&E 63.3 - software 135.0 = 694.9. FY2025 OCF also carried a $57.4M final deemed-repatriation (TCJA transition) tax installment that does not recur. CSV capex for FY2022 (128.2) disagrees with the FY2023 10-K (174.2 incl. software) -- left for the financial-parser to review. NET DEBT: cash $850.7M + short-term investments $576.2M (US Treasuries explicitly pre-funding the Nov-2026 and Sep-2027 note maturities, so treated as cash) against $3,510.3M debt (current $893.9M + long-term $2,616.4M). Interest income is not stripped from the base: the company is in net debt and the component build is unlevered (EBITDA-based), so no interest flows sit in the projections. BUYBACKS: $0 in FY2024-FY2025; $149.3M in 9M FY2026 under the new $1.0B authorization, FY2026 target raised to $400M -- Hasbro is now a funding repurchaser, so the flat count is being paid for. TARIFF REFUNDS: $54.5M IEEPA recovery booked in Q3 FY2026 cost of sales (plus ~$13M expected) is one-off; the year-2 margin step-down removes it.

historical_growth.owner_fcf_series_basis: OCF - PP&E additions - software development additions - SBC add-back - equity-award withholding taxes. FY2021-FY2023 PP&E figures from the FY2023 10-K include software; FY2024-FY2025 sum the two lines from the FY2025 10-K.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Historical CAGRs are not usable as a growth anchor. Revenue CAGRs are depressed by the eOne Film/TV and Music divestitures (2021-2023; eOne contributed ~$1.0B/yr of revenue). Equity CAGRs are destroyed by $1.19B (FY2023) and $1.02B (FY2025) goodwill impairments plus a ~$390M/yr dividend in excess of earnings. EPS is negative in FY2023 and FY2025, so EPS CAGRs are undefined. The 3-year owner-FCF CAGR (86%) starts from a FY2022 trough (working-capital build, $408M program production spend at eOne). Selected rate is the base path's long-run average (~3.5%), not a historical CAGR.
historical_growth.notes: SBC-adjusted owner-FCF 5-year CAGR (-5.8%) is below reported FCF (-0.5%) because both SBC-incl-taxes and software capex rose while FY2020 OCF was inflated by a COVID-era working-capital release; reported FCF additionally omits software capex. The FY2025 base excludes nothing: the $57.4M final repatriation-tax installment depresses it.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +9%: top of the raised 7-9% cc range plus a small FX tailwind; 9M FY2026 is already +14.7%, so Q4 at this rate is down ~6% against a record Q4 FY2025. FY2027 +2%: Magic laps two years of Universes Beyond (Final Fantasy, Marvel, Avatar) records, partly offset by the Harry Potter toy license starting 2027. Then low-to-mid single digit: Wizards mid-single digit, Consumer Products roughly flat, licensing growing.
base.ebitda_margin_rationale: FY2026 guided adj. EBITDA $1.575-1.625B on ~$5.12B revenue = ~31%, which includes ~$55-68M of one-off IEEPA tariff refunds. Year 2 steps down to 30% to remove them and absorb Harry Potter royalty cost; mature 30.5% holds rather than expands because amortisation of capitalised digital-game spend starts hitting cost of sales as titles release (2027+), offsetting further Wizards mix gains and the last $200M of the $1B cost programme.
base.capex_rationale: Capex = PP&E (tooling) + capitalised software. FY2025 4.2% of revenue ($198M); FY2026 guided ~$250M (~4.9%), 9M actual $148.5M, so 4.6%. Fades to 3.2% as the digital-game pipeline matures and its cost shifts into amortisation inside EBITDA (charging it as capex AND amortisation at the same time would double count).
base.tax_rationale: 9M FY2026 cash taxes ($82.5M) are low on OBBBA immediate R&D expensing; ramps to ~21% (US federal + state + foreign mix, Pillar-2 safe-harbour) by year 3.
base.wc_rationale: Toy wholesaler: receivables + inventory + prepaid ($1,812M) exceed payables + accrued ($1,420M) -> NWC ~8% of revenue, consumed by growth.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2026 lands at the top of the raised guide (~$5.1B revenue, ~31% adj. EBITDA margin including one-off tariff refunds). Magic: The Gathering then digests two record Universes Beyond years -- FY2027 grows only ~2% as Final Fantasy/Marvel comps bite, cushioned by the Harry Potter toy license -- before Wizards settles into mid-single-digit growth on the annual set cadence and MTG Arena. Consumer Products is roughly flat (toy category mature, tariffs a wash after the IEEPA ruling), licensing (Monopoly Go!, location-based entertainment) grows. Margin holds ~30.5%: Wizards mix and the remaining cost savings are offset by amortisation of the new owned digital titles. Capex fades from the ~$250M FY2026 peak as the game pipeline matures.
scenario_narratives.bull: Magic proves structural rather than cyclical: Universes Beyond keeps widening the collector base (The Hobbit, further crossovers), the 2027+ owned digital titles (Exodus, Warlock) and Larian/Scopely partnerships add a second profit engine, and Harry Potter plus Voltron/Street Fighter licensing lift Consumer Products back to growth. Revenue compounds 5-7% for three years and the margin reaches 33% on Wizards/licensing mix and the full $1B cost programme. The market's ~20x EV/FCF is earned and an 18x exit is justified.
scenario_narratives.bear: FY2026 is a Magic peak. Universes Beyond fatigue and secondary-market saturation (the 'segmentation' class action is a symptom of the debate) cut Wizards revenue ~15% in FY2027 off the record base, Consumer Products resumes its 2024-2025 decline as tariffs return under different authority and Amazon/Walmart (20% of revenue) destock, and a digital title fails. Revenue falls ~8% over two years, margin compresses to 26% as high-margin Magic deleverages against a fixed cost base, and the business re-rates to a 12x mature toy-and-games multiple. The ~$3.5B of debt is serviceable throughout, so this is a de-rating, not a solvency case.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 20% because profit is concentrated in one franchise (Wizards ~70%+ of segment operating profit) that is running at record levels after two years of crossover-driven growth, so mean reversion is a live risk rather than a tail. Base 50% because FY2026 is nine-twelfths reported and management has guided to 'continued growth in 2027'. Bull trimmed to 30% because it needs Magic to stay at peak AND the unproven owned digital titles to succeed AND Consumer Products to turn.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF on an unlevered component build: SBC including withholding taxes fully expensed, share count held flat, capitalised software development treated as capex (the CSV's reported FCF omits it). The valuation question is how much of the FY2025-FY2026 Magic: The Gathering surge is durable; the scenario spread is mostly a bet on Wizards' FY2027-FY2028 trajectory, not on the toy business.
key_risks_to_valuation: Magic: The Gathering concentration -- a Universes Beyond hangover would hit the highest-margin revenue first
Owned digital-game slate (Exodus, Warlock, 2027+) -- capitalised spend with a $56.4M impairment already taken in Q2 FY2026
Tariff regime -- IEEPA refunds are one-off; replacement tariffs on China/Vietnam sourcing would reverse the FY2026 tailwind
Customer concentration -- Amazon 11% and Walmart 9% of revenue
Terminal value carries most of the value and the cap (15x base) binds below Gordon (~17x), so exit-multiple judgement matters
